topic: Thermodynamics and Kinetic Theory of Gases (KTG)
description: This module explores the relationships between heat, work, temperature, and energy. It bridges the microscopic behavior of gas molecules (Kinetic Theory) with the macroscopic fundamental laws governing heat transfer (Thermodynamics), which are high-yield areas for NEET and JEE.

sections.title: Thermal Properties and Calorimetry
sections.description: The study of the effects of heat on matter, temperature measurement, and the quantitative calculation of heat transfer between bodies.

key_concepts.explanation: The amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of a unit mass (1 kg or 1 g) of a substance by 1°C (or 1 K).
The amount of heat required to change the state of a substance (e.g., solid to liquid, or liquid to gas) without any change in its temperature.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Heat lost by a hot body = Heat gained by a cold body.
scientific_principles.application: Based on the law of conservation of energy, this principle is used to calculate the final equilibrium temperature of a mixture or to determine the specific heat of an unknown substance.

sections.title: Laws of Thermodynamics
sections.description: The fundamental physical laws that dictate the exchange of energy between a system and its surroundings.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: If two thermodynamic systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, then they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.
scientific_principles.application: This law rigorously defines the concept of 'Temperature' and forms the theoretical basis for constructing thermometers.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW (Heat supplied to a system equals the increase in its internal energy plus the work done by the system).
scientific_principles.application: Essentially the law of conservation of energy applied to thermal systems. It is extensively used to analyze isothermal, adiabatic, isobaric, and isochoric processes.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Kelvin-Planck Statement: It is impossible to construct an engine operating in a cycle that converts all heat completely into work. Clausius Statement: Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body without external work.
scientific_principles.application: Dictates the direction of heat flow and establishes the absolute limit on the efficiency of any heat engine (it can never be 100%).

sections.title: Heat Engines and Refrigerators
sections.description: Devices that convert heat energy into mechanical work, or use mechanical work to transfer heat against its natural gradient.

historical_events.event: Proposal of the 'Carnot Cycle' by Nicolas Léonard Sadi Carnot
historical_events.significance: He introduced a theoretical model for an ideal, reversible heat engine, which became crucial for the development of the Second Law of Thermodynamics.

key_concepts.explanation: A theoretical, ideal heat engine that operates on the Carnot cycle. It has the maximum possible efficiency of any engine working between two given temperatures (Source and Sink). Efficiency (η) = 1 - (T_sink / T_source).
A heat engine working in reverse. It utilizes external work (like electricity) to extract heat from a cold reservoir (sink) and reject it to a hot reservoir (source).

sections.title: Kinetic Theory of Gases (KTG)
sections.description: Explaining the macroscopic properties of gases (such as pressure, volume, and temperature) based on the microscopic motion of gas molecules.

key_concepts.explanation: A theoretical gas composed of point particles that do not exert intermolecular forces on each other, and whose volume is negligible compared to the container. It strictly obeys the equation PV = nRT.
The square root of the average of the squares of the velocities of all gas molecules. Formula: V_rms = √(3RT/M). It is directly proportional to the square root of the absolute temperature.

The number of independent ways in which a dynamic system (like a molecule) can possess energy (translational, rotational, or vibrational). For a monoatomic gas, f = 3; for a rigid diatomic gas, f = 5.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: For a dynamic system in thermal equilibrium, the total energy is distributed equally amongst all the active degrees of freedom, and the energy associated with each molecule per degree of freedom is (1/2)kT.
scientific_principles.application: Used to theoretically calculate the internal energy of gases and derive their molar specific heat capacities (Cp and Cv).

important_facts.fact: At Absolute Zero (0 K or -273.15°C), all translational kinetic energy of gas molecules becomes theoretically zero, meaning molecular motion completely ceases.
The pressure exerted by a gas on the walls of its container is macroscopically a result of the continuous microscopic collisions of gas molecules with the walls, causing a change in momentum.
